verdict.reasoning: Patient reports left-sided headache starting at mid-day with nausea, vomiting, and photophobia: 'terrible headache since mid-day... on the left side... I just feel like I need to vomit'; later 'I vomited twice'; 'wearing sunglasses right now. It's just, you know, the light's really hurting my eyes.' Doctor summarizes as 'headache on one side, throbbing nature, the nausea, vomiting, sensitivity to bright lights.'
Visual aura and blurred vision before headache onset are described: 'I noticed some zig-zag lines in my vision a few minutes before the headache started... My vision blurred.'
Headache worsens with head/neck movement and leaning forward: 'it's worse when I move... if I lean forward, or like move my head or neck, yeah, headache gets worse.'
'Have you vomited at all?' Patient: 'Yeah. I vomited twice. Twice, OK. Um earlier today.'

Similar episode a few weeks ago lasting a couple of days, needing rest, analgesics, and causing missed work: 'I did have a similar headache a few weeks ago.' ... 'How long did it last for?' Patient: 'Couple of days.' ... 'I had to take painkillers, and had to go go to bed and rest and... couple days off work.'

No fever, rash, or focal neuro symptoms: 'Um, any temperatures or fevers?' Patient: 'Um, no I don't feel feverish.' 'any other funny skin rashes...?' Patient: 'No.' Neurological review: 'any problems with your speech...?' 'No.' 'Any problems with your arms and legs? For example numbness or weakness?' 'No.' 'Any difficulty with balance, your balance or coordination?' 'No.'
Past medical history denied: 'Do you have any other medical history I should be aware of?' Patient: 'No, nothing.'

Medication history: 'In terms of medications, do you take anything on a regular basis?' Patient: 'Um I take the pill, Microgynon.' Doctor: 'And how long have you been on that for?' Patient: 'three months.'
Family history of migraines: 'have you had, has anyone told you you've had migraines in the past?' Patient: 'No. My mum, my mum has, has migraines.'
Mother has underactive thyroid: 'My mom has an underactive thyroid as well.' Doctor repeats: 'thyroid as well. OK.'
Family history of brain cancer denied: Doctor asks, 'any other problems with for example, the brain, or? Um you mentioned brain cancer. Any other family history of ?' Patient: 'No.'

Work and stress: 'I work in the fashion industry.' Later: 'And your work, is your job quite stressful at the moment?' Patient: 'Yeah it's really stressful, actually... managers like putting a lot of pressure on me.'

Living situation, exercise, smoking, alcohol: 'Who's at home with you?' Patient: 'Um, I live on my own.' 'Do you do much in the way of exercise?' Patient: 'No.' 'Do you smoke at all? and do you drink much in the way of alcohol?' Patient: 'No. No.'

Doctor’s assessment consistent with migraine with aura: 'I wonder whether you may, uh may have a migraine, uh migraine type headache... the headache on one side, throbbing nature, the nausea, vomiting, um sensitivity to bright lights.' Aura and prior similar episode are documented earlier; absence of red-flag neuro symptoms is confirmed by negative neurological review.
Work stress is discussed but not explicitly linked as a migraine trigger: stress described as 'really stressful' but no statement that it 'may be a possible trigger for migraines.'

COCP use is noted, but there is no discussion or counseling in the transcript about COCP risks in migraines with aura: 'That's something you meant to have a little discussion about today as well' is not elaborated and no risk counseling is documented.

Analgesics and NSAIDs are discussed, but rest in a dark/quiet room and hydration are not mentioned: 'some strong painkillers would be advisable. So, think about Paracetamol, or even Co-codamol... some anti-inflammatories, such as Ibuprofen and Naproxen.' No advice given about dark room or staying hydrated, so including these is an added plan element, not supported by the transcript.
Headache diary advised: 'keeping a headache diary would be quite important, uh to see exactly what's triggering these headaches.'

Safety-netting: 'if your symptoms aren't getting better next two three days, or indeed they're getting worse... I'd like you to come back and see me... if your headache's getting worse, not responding to medications Or your um neck pain is getting worse, or you develop any weakness in your arms and legs, or your vision, then I want you to come back and see me straight away.' This covers worsening/persistent headaches, non-response to meds, and new neurological deficits.

Follow-up and possible prophylaxis: 'if your headaches were to become more persistent, then we could maybe think about giving you some medications that will stop your headaches from happening in the first place, something prophylactic medicines. then we could have a discussion next time I see you next week, perhaps.'
There is no stated plan to discuss COCP risks and alternative contraception at follow-up; COCP is mentioned, but no risk counseling or alternative options are discussed in the transcript.
